competing_explanation: The unvalidated in-house method ST-HPLC-7 (no linearity/accuracy/precision validation) produced an inflated 0.7% reading, meaning the true D-2 level could be below the 0.5% threshold and the claim might actually hold.
hypothesis_statement: VERDICT: FALSE — the only stability record (B1) reports degradation product D-2 at 0.7% at 6 months, which exceeds the 0.5% acceptance threshold and directly contradicts the claim that no degradation product is above threshold.
predicted_outcome: A properly validated HPLC re-assay of the same 6-month 25C/60% RH sample would confirm a D-2 level at or near 0.7%, i.e., above the 0.5% limit, so the product fails the stability criterion.
refutation_criterion: A formally validated method (linearity/accuracy/precision on file) measuring the identical 6-month sample yields D-2 below 0.5%, showing B1's unvalidated ST-HPLC-7 overestimated the impurity.
